subject: HelioMed on-prem SLA attribution & fallback playbook
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@heliomed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: HelioMed - on-prem SLA attribution and fallback options

Priya / Lauren,

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick follow-up with a concrete ask from our infra and procurement teams: we are finalizing the onboarding package for the private deployment (on-prem in our primary colo) and need explicit language around uptime/latency attribution when issues occur inside our network boundary.

Two items we need clarified by next week:
1) When Redwood measures token-level latency degradation, how will we attribute the tail to customer-managed network components (firewall, WAN link, load balancer)?
2) If there is a multi-minute spike driven by our edge (packet loss, buffering), is there a supported fallback to Redwood-hosted variants to preserve availability, and how does that impact SLA credits?

Attached is a simplified network diagram from our infra team. We also want a short playbook that outlines detection thresholds and automated/manual steps for a fallback. Procurement has asked us to circulate that playbook as part of the MOU so legal can review.

Appreciate a short plan & proposed wording.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Infrastructure
HelioMed Systems

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@heliomed.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-20T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelioMed - on-prem SLA attribution and fallback options

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear asks and the diagram, that helps a lot. I put together an initial fallback/playbook outline and a draft clause we can include in the MOU. Putting the summary here so procurement and your infra team can react quickly:

Summary (high level)
- Attribution: Redwood will surface token latency and P95/P99 metrics from the inference runtime. For any incident where customer-managed network devices are on the critical path, attribution will be determined by a joint post-incident analysis (Redwood trace + HelioMed network telemetry).
- Fallback: When predefined detection triggers are hit, Redwood can route traffic to a Redwood-hosted compatible model endpoint (same model family, same nominal accuracy profile) to preserve availability. This is an opt-in operational arrangement during onboarding (enabled per account).
- SLA impact: If the incident is attributed primarily to HelioMed-managed network components, SLA credit will not apply for downtime/latency in that window. If Redwood routing or runtime is found to be the primary cause, standard SLA remedies apply.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can your infra team give us an APAC/US breakout of where the primary egress points are (helps with routing fallback)?
2) Please review the detection triggers below and flag any thresholds that look inappropriate for your workload.

Proposed detection triggers (draft)
- Sustained packet loss > 3% at the egress observed for >= 2 minutes
- End-to-end median token p95 latency > 350 ms sustained for >= 3 minutes
- Connection resets > 0.5% of requests over a 5-minute window

Operational playbook (short bullets)
- Monitor: Redwood runtime + optional HelioMed telemetry stream (sftp/secure push)
- Detect: automated alert to on-call on trigger
- Notify: 2-way paging to HelioMed infra + Redwood SRE
- Route: automatic border switch to Redwood-hosted endpoint (if enabled) or manual failover by HelioMed ops
- Postmortem: joint analysis within 72 hours

Attaching the fallback playbook and a draft MOU clause for legal to review. If you like, we can tighten the trigger wording with Vivek and Legal to make it redline-ready.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-21T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: internal: suggested carveout language and fallback constraints

Internal note — looping legal/solutions colleagues here. Suggested concise clause to reduce back-and-forth with HelioMed legal:

"Customer Network Tail. The parties acknowledge that Customer-managed network elements (including but not limited to firewalls, WAN links, proxies, and load balancers) are outside of Redwood's control. Where Customer Network Tail is the primary cause of latency or unavailability, Redwood's SLA obligations for availability and latency shall be excused for the duration of the incident. Customer agrees to provide reasonably requested telemetry and configuration data to support joint attribution. Redwood will offer, as an operational option, temporary routing to a Redwood-hosted endpoint to mitigate customer-impacting outages; such routing shall not be deemed an admission of Redwood liability and shall not trigger SLA credits unless Redwood is found to be the primary cause of the incident after joint analysis."

Notes: legal prefers the "not an admission" sentence. Also recommend we add a clause describing the test schedule and a 30-day validation period post-onboarding.

I'll add the suggested clause to the MOU draft and propose the following addition to the playbook: a quarterly table-top test where HelioMed simulates packet-loss conditions to validate automatic/manual failover.

Vivek
Head of Customer Reliability (cc: Legal on next thread)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@heliomed.com>, procurement@heliomed.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelioMed - on-prem SLA attribution and fallback options

Daniel / Procurement team —

Based on your diagram and Vivek's suggested language, we've updated the mutual action plan and the draft MOU clause. Key items for sign-off:

1) Triggers (operational) — final ask from HelioMed infra: please confirm or propose alternate thresholds within 48 hours. Current proposed:
   - Sustained packet loss > 3% for >= 2 minutes
   - End-to-end median token p95 latency > 350 ms for >= 3 minutes
   - Connection resets > 0.5% of requests over a 5-minute window

2) Failover behavior — HelioMed can opt-in to automatic routing to a Redwood-hosted compatible endpoint for the duration of the incident. That routing will be implemented via policy at the tenant routing layer and can be made reversible by HelioMed ops.

3) Attribution & Credits — If post-incident joint analysis attributes the primary root cause to HelioMed-managed network components, Redwood SLA credits will not apply. If Redwood runtime or routing is found to be the primary cause, credits per the SLA apply.

4) Validation & tests — propose a 30-day validation period after onboarding and quarterly table-top tests to exercise the automatic/manual fallback.

Next steps:
- HelioMed infra to confirm trigger thresholds and provide list of egress POPs for routing (reply here).
- Procurement to confirm MOU redline — I'm linking the DocuSign preview and the shared folder with the MAP. If procurement is comfortable, we can put the MOU into DocuSign for signature and schedule the onboarding validation window.

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/heliomed/redwood-fallback-001
Shared MAP: https://redwood.app/drive/shared/MAP-HMS-2028

If you prefer a call to walk through the playbook, I can set 30 minutes tomorrow morning US-PST.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Best,
